/about/our-story: Parnell Cricket Club has been affiliated since 1883 and over the years has produced many fine players. Since 1996 the Club has been based at the Shore Road Reserve in Remuera and neighbouring Bloodworth Park. Facilities include clubrooms, changing rooms and outdoor nets at Shore Road plus a pavilion and outdoor nets at Bloodworth Park, and the recently completed Terry Jarvis Indoor Training Centre with three indoor nets.

Parnell CC dates back to 1858 and is the oldest club in New Zealand. Both daily papers, ‘The New Zealander’ and the ‘Southern Cross’ recorded a game between Parnell and Auckland on Wednesday, 17 March 1858, at Albert Barracks.
For the record, Parnell won by an innings and 28 runs – our team of teenagers, labelled in the Press as ‘the Juveniles’, bowled Auckland out for only 11 in their elders’ second innings.

That Parnell side remained together for several seasons. Then they set about establishing the game around the country. Auckland challenged and beat Wellington in 1860 – 5 Parnell members were in that first Auckland side. Two members helped establish Otago cricket and were instrumental in setting up:
NZ’s first 1st Class match Jan. 1864 – Otago vs. Canterbury (Parnell’s John Kissling umpired, GK Turton played)
The first international games – Geo. Parr’s All England XI vs. XXIIs of Otago and Canterbury

Back in Auckland cricket slowly developed – the Domain, thanks to Parnell players taking the initiative, was partly cleared for a field. And overseas teams came again – Lillywhite’s All England XI in 1876/77 and the Australians in 1877/7. Auckland Cricket Association was finally formed in 1883 and Parnell affiliated with it in 1884. Over the next decade Australian and English visited frequently and the Domain, where Parnell played along with all the other clubs, was considered one of the most beautiful in the Southern Hemisphere.

Club cricket blossomed in the 1890s with Parnell winning the Championship twice. However, the Club really came into its own when, under the new District Scheme, Parnell won the Championship 5 times between 1898 and 1914. Notable Parnell players were Ike Mills, the outstanding Auckland and NZ bat, and Cay Olliff, a prolific leg break bowler. Administrators, too, Fred Earl and Bob Lusk proved to be outstanding not only for the Club but also in the setting up of Eden Park and for Auckland and NZ Cricket. And Bill Dinnison joined the Club, almost immediately became Secretary and, from then, ensured that the Club ran without a hitch for decade after decade.

Between the two World Wars, Parnell produced players of outstanding caliber including Paul Whitelaw, Merv Wallace and Giff Vivian. Then Bert Sutcliffe, straight from Takapuna Grammar, joined in 1940/41, possibly our greatest batsman ever. After WW2, Johnny Hayes spearheaded our attack and, too, was selected by NZ to tour England in 1949 and 1958.

For years the Club sought a permanent Home Ground. After the Domain, Eden Park was our base to WW2, then back to the Domain. In 1950 Hobson Park became available and we were there till 1966, a marvelous nursery for young elite cricketers – Ross Morgan, Bill Playle, Mark Burgess, Terry Jarvis and others grew up there under the watchful eyes of Merv Wallace and Geoff Rabone and superb administrators such as Peter Badley and Jack Forsman.

Hobson Park was lost to summer hockey so, from 1966, we had to ’make do’ at Eden Park till moving to Orakei Domain in 1984. This isolated Seniors from our Juniors until, in 2001/02, Auckland City Council invited us to re-locate to the newly reclaimed Shore Road Reserve. The rest is history – a 5 bay outdoor net complex and clubroom quickly built then the Terry Jarvis Centre, a state of the art practice facility. Best of all, a proper amalgamation of the administrations of our Junior and Senior Sections into a governing Board.

/about/our-ambition: Parnell Cricket Club (PCC) is NZ's oldest cricket club and was established in 1858.
Over many years we have evolved into one of Auckland’s most successful cricket clubs.

The club has over 750 players, including 600+ juniors. We have a rich history of success with over 40 past and current NZ representatives including 2 current BLACKCAPS and 8 current First Class players in our membership.
We are equally passionate about the male and female, junior, youth and senior grades and have passionate administrators driving for success on all fronts.

PCC was Auckland Cricket’s Club of the Year in the 2019/20 and 2020/21 seasons and again in the 2023 / 24 season, where we have had arguably our most successful Senior Club season ever with wins in the Auckland Premier Men’s T20 competition, winning both the Auckland Women’s Premier One Day and T20 competitions as well as the Premier Reserve Womens T20 grade.
COMMUNITY | BE BRAVE | BE OUR BEST | PASSION | RESPECT

Safety and wellbeing of all PCC members and the wider community is a priority for PCC. Parnell Cricket Club has zero tolerance for illicit drug possession and/or use by playing members, club affiliated persons and members of the community during PCC activities and/or at PCC premises. Any activities or alleged activities in breach of this policy will be treated as matter for review under the PCC Code of Conduct and may result in disciplinary steps. Any concerns or questions about this policy should be referred to the PCC Director of Cricket.

/grade/junior-boys-mixed-grades: Skill development & Team Trainings. This grade focuses on introducing the fundamentals of cricket in a fun, engaging, and safe environment. Emphasizing skill development, sportsmanship, and team play, the junior grade provides an excellent foundation for young enthusiasts to learn and grow in the sport.

Each Parnell Junior Club team is allocated regular pro-coach led sessions in addition to their own team coach led session. With a range of age-specific teams and coaching sessions, the club ensures that each child receives the right level of training and competition, making their early cricketing experience both enjoyable and rewarding.

Players are allocated to club teams based on their school year: Year 0-4, then Under 10 Years through to Under 13. Beyond weekend club cricket, players have the opportunity to join club representative teams to compete in the Hawkes Bay Summer Camps, JT Sparling Series and U13 Club Summer Series.

/grade/youth-boy: Whether you’re new to cricket or have a few seasons under your belt, Parnell’s Youth Boys program is dedicated to providing a supportive and competitive environment. Our experienced coaching team ensures each player receives the attention they need to develop their skills and enjoy the game.

/grade/mens: Parnell Cricket Club’s Senior Men’s program caters to players seeking competitive cricket and strong team camaraderie. Our programme focuses on high-level skill enhancement and match preparedness.‍

Parnell Cricket Club has a Premier Men's, Premier Reserves, and Premier Thirds side, each playing in the Major competition of their respective division. The teams represent the club in the Auckland Cricket Competition which runs from October through to the end of March. The Competition includes all three formats of the game: Two Day cricket, One Day cricket along with T20 cricket. We may also have a 4XI depending on numbers.

The PCC teams are high performing, with the Premier side having won multiple trophies in recent years, and the club winning the Simmonds and Osborne trophy three times in recent seasons. The Club aims to create a high performing but fun culture, with players enjoying the game as well as the team and club environment.
Pre-season starts in late August/Early September. More details will be provided on registration.‍

‍Training & CoachingSenior Men’s trainings for the Prems, Reserves and Thirds are held at Shore Road (often in the TJC indoor nets – ensuring we can train even in wet weather) on Tuesday and Thursday evenings led by our Pro-Coaches. All three sides have dedicated team coaches.‍
Aside from the Premier grades noted above, we also offer other playing opportunities.‍

PresidentsThis grade caters to older players (Over 35’s) who still wish to play competitive cricket. Matches are one-day games held on Saturday afternoons, starting in early November and running through to the end of March. Practices for our Presidents team are on every Wednesday evening from 6pm-even during the winter months!‍

Parnell Cricket have a number of competitive Championship teams along with a number of One day teams available to join. These teams play throughout the season from Labour weekend till the end of March.
Parnell has a very keen and enthusiastic Presidents side that caters for the older (Over 35) player who still wishes to play competitive cricket

1. Pressure- Walk towards or walk away2. IDENTITY- THE GOLDEN THREAD OF MENTAL SKILLS3. Outcome verses Process4. Courage5. Fear Verses Freedom6. Authenticity verses compromise‍

/facility/terry-jarvis-centre: The Terry Jarvis Centre is a purpose built, indoor sports facility designed for a variety of indoor uses. The initiators and fundraisers for the facility were Parnell Cricket Club who have set the facility up for both cricket use as well as a variety of other indoor sports. With three internationally specified cricket lanes as well as the opportunity to be able to retract the nets to create a large open and unrestricted space for training and practice sessions the facility will have a number of uses whether you are an aspiring international cricketer, school or local community group.
The centre is managed and operated by the Parnell Cricket Club on behalf of the Remuera Parnell Sports Community Charitable Trust.
